drill_library.title: John Jay Varsity — Drill Library
drill_library.html:
John Jay Varsity — Drill Library

Built for Coachy 60-minute ADM practice plans. Each entry has a short written setup and a public video URL (YouTube or Vimeo).

Where the drills webpage lives

  • Hub John Jay drill strip (6 IceHockeySystems Shorts): https://bottz77.github.io/franks-hub/#/johnjay
  • Private twin: https://franks-hub-private.pages.dev/#/johnjay
  • Config: `frank-hub/feeds.json` → `johnjay.videos` → IceHockeySystems
  • jjpuck.com Resources: menu exists but has no drill pages (empty). Club site is schedules/roster only.
  • Expanded sources: icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills, ADM Drill of the Month, USA Hockey articles.

Inventory: 38 drills with video links, plus 30 `one-goalie` additions (#39–68, added 2026-10-06). Machine-readable full scrape: `jj_drill_library.json` (54 entries).

Tags: `warm-up` | `skills` | `contact` | `sag` | `systems` | `goalie` | `one-goalie`

1. 1v1 Race to the Puck → 3v3 Transition Drill

  • Tags: `contact|sag`
  • Directions: Start with a 1v1 race to a dumped puck, then layer into 3v3 transition as support arrives. Teaches win-the-puck-line body position, then immediate support and transition. Keep the whistle cadence high.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/lZgVOd8_TSI
  • Source page: https://bottz77.github.io/franks-hub/#/johnjay

2. 2 v 2 Angle Half-Ice Hockey Game with Defensive Reward

  • Tags: `contact|sag`
  • Directions: Half-ice 2v2 with angling focus and a defensive reward rule (e.g., clear/score after a takeaway). Offense must move to support; defense angles first, then stick, then body. Continuous short shifts so everyone gets reps.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/PfpCL35u1tY
  • Source page: https://bottz77.github.io/franks-hub/#/johnjay

3. 1 v 1 Angle & Gap Full Ice Hockey Drill

  • Tags: `contact|skills`
  • Directions: Full-ice 1v1 emphasizing angle and gap. Defender closes on an angle (stick on ice, outside shoulder lined up) while the attacker reads pressure and attacks open ice. Keep shifts short; reward the defender for forcing outside and the attacker for protecting the puck through contact.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/WvmJ8qkkOn8
  • Source page: https://bottz77.github.io/franks-hub/#/johnjay

4. 3 v 3 Play Fast Game that Involves the WHOLE TEAM

  • Tags: `sag|skills`
  • Directions: Full-team 3v3 play-fast small-area game. Keep all lines rotating with short shifts so nobody stands. Emphasize first touch, immediate support, and transition the instant possession changes.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/8loIyjdiosg
  • Source page: https://bottz77.github.io/franks-hub/#/johnjay

5. 2 v 2 Transition Hockey Game from NHL Development Camp

  • Tags: `sag|systems`
  • Directions: 2v2 transition game used in NHL development camp. Offense attacks; on turnover, both sides transition immediately. Cue quick feet, first pass under pressure, and D activating or recovering without watching.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/041oIbGpvvg
  • Source page: https://bottz77.github.io/franks-hub/#/johnjay

6. What it means to be a good leader with Gold Medalist Hayley Scamurra

  • Tags: `systems`
  • Directions: Team talk / leadership clip. Use as a 60–90 second board or locker-room cue on compete, accountability, and how leaders set the tone for practice and games. Not an on-ice drill—pair with a compete block the same night.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/wwOIUxHVMTw
  • Source page: https://bottz77.github.io/franks-hub/#/johnjay

7. New Jersey 1v1 / 2v2 Contact SAG

  • Tags: `contact|sag`
  • Directions: Below-hash or half-zone boxes. Dump a puck; 1v1 then 2v2 with legal contact taught that night. Winner exits to a shot. Stop illegal hits immediately. Angle first, stick second, body third.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/PfpCL35u1tY
  • Source page: https://www.usahockey.com/trainingmaterials

8. 1 v 1 Use The Net

  • Tags: `contact|skills`
  • Directions: 1 v 1 Use the Net from Jason Lammers is a great drill for all age levels that encourages offensive awareness and puck protection while the defenders work on angling and proper stick detail. The offensive team is trying to skate the puck through the gate while the defender is looking to strip the puck and score on net. Setup Setup a net and a gate as the goals.
  • Video: https://vimeo.com/1154377465
  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/1-v-1-use-net

9. Angle Behind Net + Stick Check

  • Tags: `contact|skills`
  • Directions: O carries behind the net; X angles to force outside/into the corner and finishes with stick lift/press or controlled rub—no open-ice charge. Switch roles every few reps. Cue: stay slightly behind until the carrier clears the net, then close.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m88qmzCcERw
  • Source page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m88qmzCcERw

10. Puck Race to Possession Game

  • Tags: `contact|skills`
  • Directions: Objective New York Sirens forward Elle Hartje teaches players that winning a puck race isn't about being first to the puck—it's about winning the puck line. This competitive puck battle game develops body positioning on puck races, puck protection under pressure, and the ability to quickly transition into offense or defense on the second whistle. Setup Coach places a puck inside one of the faceoff circles.
  • Video: https://vimeo.com/1210465912
  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/puck-race-possession-game

11. Pioneer 2 V 2 Rush

  • Tags: `contact|systems`
  • Directions: The Pioneer 2 V 2 Rush from TJ Manastersky , the Head Coach of Brock University , practices attacking and defending the rush. It starts as a 1 V 1, and finishes as a 2 V 2. Setup On the 1st whistle, blue passes to red.
  • Video: https://vimeo.com/784999967
  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/pioneer-2-v-2-rush

12. Partner Bump / Controlled Contact Confidence

  • Tags: `contact|warm-up`
  • Directions: Size-matched pairs. Side-by-side knees bent: 3 strides → shoulder/hip bump → continue; both directions. Lead with shoulder not head, elbows in, stick on ice. Half-speed first, then add a puck and board-side bumps. Contact every practice.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jai0vHhRuEY
  • Source page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jai0vHhRuEY

13. Practice Goalie Shuffles & Edgework with No Crease

  • Tags: `goalie|skills`
  • Directions: Goalie edgework and shuffles that do not require a painted crease—use cones or boards. Pair with skater stations so Liam gets focused movement work while others rotate.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EASYdYzvucU
  • Source page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EASYdYzvucU

14. 2 vs 2 Rebound Battle Hockey Game

  • Tags: `sag|goalie|skills`
  • Directions: 2v2 battle off rebound looks. Coach or shooter creates a rebound; both pairs compete for second chances and net-front body position. Excellent goalie tracking volume.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FtXlcBl3D2I
  • Source page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FtXlcBl3D2I

15. 3 on 3 Play Fast Small Area Hockey Game

  • Tags: `sag|skills`
  • Directions: Classic IHS 3v3 play-fast SAG. Short shifts, continuous play, reward speed of support after a pass. Pair with the Hub Short of the same theme for a quick visual before the whistle.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DK_N5S36_oE
  • Source page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DK_N5S36_oE

16. Corner Tires - Small Area Game

  • Tags: `sag|skills`
  • Directions: Corner Tires is a small area game where the players score by hitting the tire with a puck. Set Up Place four tires on a rectangle as shown in the diagram. Make sure there is enough room from the tires to the edge so that there is room to play on all sides of the tires.
  • Video: https://vimeo.com/410680521
  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/corner-tires-small-area-game

17. Corner to Half Wall 2 vs 1

  • Tags: `sag|skills`
  • Directions: The Corner to Half Wall 2 vs 1 is an excellent small area game for all age levels that helps players practice a 2 vs 1 in a small space along the boards in the corner of the ice. The game reinforces important skills like keeping your head up, moving to open spaces, protecting the puck, and verbal & non-verbal communication. Offensive players should practice using the boards to make bank passes.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hnLu_shT2J0
  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/corner-half-wall-2-vs-1

18. Gates of Buffalo Small Area Passing Game

  • Tags: `sag|skills`
  • Directions: The major concept of the Gates of Buffalo Small Area Hockey Game is to practice moving to open space, communicating verbally and non-verbally with teammates, so they can score Goals by passing through Gates. This game framework will help players learn to play with their head up, communicate with teammates and move to open space. As a coach, If you commit to working on activities like this instead of memorization drills for a portion of each practice, you will marvel at how your team begins to work together.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JlKKAFlVTLc
  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/gates-buffalo-small-area-game

19. Hit The Tire Passing Game WIth No Goalie

  • Tags: `sag|skills`
  • Directions: Hit The Tire Passing Game is a fun small area game that can be utilized when coaches want to work on passing and puck support concepts and/or there are no goalies available. Setup Place a tire on each of the face-off dots inside of a zone. The offensive team scores by hitting the tire in the opposite circle.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9LZa7cH-phw
  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/hit-tire-passing-game-no-goalie

20. Ramsay 3 V 3 Race

  • Tags: `sag|skills`
  • Directions: Jason Lammers describes the Ramsay 3 V 3 Race. This competitive small area game incorporates racing to the puck to determine which team is on offense. Setup Full ice setup with goalies in both nets.
  • Video: https://vimeo.com/861028778
  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/ramsay-3-v-3-race

21. Swedish 2 vs 1 (Cross Ice)

  • Tags: `sag|skills`
  • Directions: This is a phenomenal drill in several ways. First, the concept of this drill can be used in many different areas of the ice. Secondly, it forces players to think 2 on 1's in tight spaces.
  • Video: https://vimeo.com/342763238
  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/swedish-2-vs-1-cross-ice

22. Buffalo 2v2 to 3v3 to 4v4

  • Tags: `sag|systems`
  • Directions: Objective A high tempo transition drill from Day 2 of the 2026 Buffalo Sabres Development Camp that Camp that starts as a 2v2 and progresses to a 3v3 and 4v4. Both teams are trying to defend & score. Setup Nets on goal line and blue line.
  • Video: https://vimeo.com/1222710175
  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/buffalo-2v2-3v3-4v4-3

23. Offense 3 v 2 Cross-ice Hockey Game

  • Tags: `sag|systems`
  • Directions: Cross-ice 3v2 that rewards quick east-west play and late support. Defense manages middle ice and sticks in lanes; offense looks for the third attacker.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MhoajOVDeGU
  • Source page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MhoajOVDeGU

24. Oreo

  • Tags: `sag|systems`
  • Directions: Oreo 3 V 3 Game from Jason Lammers is a continuous game that is competitive in nature as it forces the defense to work to pass the puck to the next players in line, while the offensive team is trying to score. Setup In this example, 3 players line up on the blue line. The players behind them are on the opposite team.
  • Video: https://vimeo.com/847506383
  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/oreo

25. Picket Fences Game (2 vs. 2 or 3 vs. 3)

  • Tags: `sag|systems`
  • Directions: Picket Fences is a great small area hockey game that can be setup as a 2 vs. The offensive team gets 2 points for scoring a goal and the defensive team gets 1 point by skating the puck between the tires . Setup: Teams are set up in one of the offensive zones in line with Dots.
  • Video: https://vimeo.com/434166992
  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/picket-fences

26. Sully 2 on 2 Transition Game

  • Tags: `sag|systems`
  • Directions: The Sully 2 on 2 Transition Game from Michael Peca was recorded during the 2024-25 NHL Season. This is a high-tempo small-area game designed to develop quick transition skills, offensive movement, and defensive awareness. The drill encourages players to convert defense into offense efficiently while emphasizing strong defensive details and communication.
  • Video: https://vimeo.com/1067058133
  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/sully-2-on-2-transition-game

27. Shooting Off The Pass - Offensive Zone Hockey Drill

  • Tags: `skills|goalie`
  • Directions: Offensive-zone timing drill: receive in motion and shoot in one action. Emphasize catch-and-release, weight transfer, and getting the puck through from tough angles. Feed Liam quality looks.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eti1cwBR978
  • Source page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eti1cwBR978

28. Use The Net 2 on 1 Hockey Drill

  • Tags: `skills|systems`
  • Directions: 2-on-1 that uses the net as a pick/screen and deception tool. Offense delays, uses the net to change sides, and looks for the late attacker; defender manages gap and stick while protecting the middle.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=e6ioQDMwYlw
  • Source page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=e6ioQDMwYlw

29. Breakout Transition Game

  • Tags: `systems`
  • Directions: Objective: a 2 v 2 game were the offense is trying to score and the defense is working hard to create turnovers and breakout by passing the puck to their teammates at center ice. Setup: Set up nets across the zone. Draw a line down the middle of the ice from the blue line to end wall.
  • Video: https://vimeo.com/1122947715
  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/breakout-transition-game

30. USA Activation Drill (14U+)

  • Tags: `systems|sag`
  • Directions: Coach shoots a puck across; first two from each line race to it while the next two become activating D behind the nets. Possession side can attack or kick back to activating D for a 4v2. Run 30-second shifts; teach battle + activate.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DK_N5S36_oE
  • Source page: https://www.usahockey.com/news_article/show/716266-14u-usa-activation-drill

31. ADM F1 Forecheck Game (10U–18U)

  • Tags: `systems|sag|contact`
  • Directions: 3v3 cross-ice with a center-line marker. After a D-zone retrieval, the team must skate behind its net before attacking. On a turnover in the attack zone, at least one F1 must pressure the puck. Reward immediate attack off a steal.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fDxI2eeEciY
  • Source page: https://www.admkids.com/news_article/show/754281-10u-18u-f1-forecheck-game

32. Backcheck Small Area Game (tracking)

  • Tags: `systems|sag|contact`
  • Directions: Two end zones and a small NZ. Attackers enter; once all four players are in the end zone, new defenders wait in NZ. Original attackers must backcheck as the other team attacks. Stress stops/starts and tracking all the way to the net.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fDxI2eeEciY
  • Source page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fDxI2eeEciY

33. NZ Give and Go

  • Tags: `systems|skills`
  • Directions: Objective Develop off-puck movement and teach players to create give-and-go opportunities by moving immediately after a pass. The game encourages players to think ahead, recognize available space, and create new passing lanes to get the puck back. 2 game in the neutral zone .
  • Video: https://vimeo.com/1223931767
  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/nz-give-and-go-1

34. Chicago 5 Puck Warm-Up Hockey Drill For Full Team

  • Tags: `warm-up|skills`
  • Directions: Full-team warm-up with five pucks moving. Players keep circulating, exchanging passes, and filling lanes so the ice stays alive. Great openers for touch, awareness, and tempo before stations.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IsD9ZDgPO0k
  • Source page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IsD9ZDgPO0k

35. Ice Hockey Passing Drill - Rondo Progressions

  • Tags: `warm-up|skills`
  • Directions: Rondo-style passing progressions (keep-away circles). Start with more attackers than defenders and shrink the outlet time. Cue one-touch options and body shape to receive.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JW2BBDdR07I
  • Source page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JW2BBDdR07I

36. Pit Chaos Handling with Passes

  • Tags: `warm-up|skills`
  • Directions: The Pit Chaos Handling With Passing drill is an excellent activity that helps players work on awareness, puck handling, and passing skills. This drill can be used as a warm-up in practice or games, or as a drill to reinforce keeping your head up. Setup Setup 2, 3, or 4 players in the middle of a face-off circle.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UxmQBKTJ2ss
  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/pit-chaos-handling-passes

37. Side Middle Side

  • Tags: `warm-up|skills`
  • Directions: The Side Middle Side passing drill from Darryl Belfry is from his practice plan, Parallel Teaching Structure - Passing Between Two Checks and One Touch Passing . This specific drill allows the whole team to warm up their skating, puck handling, passing and vision at the beginning of the practice. Setup Players line up at all 4 neutral zone face-off circles with pucks.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yeRHZLK2eek
  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/side-middle-side-passing

38. Defensive Transition Passing Warm-Up Drill for Hockey Players

  • Tags: `warm-up|systems`
  • Directions: Warm-up flow that links retrievals to first-pass exits. Skaters retrieve, hit a support target, and transition up ice without standing still. Great for D breakout habits.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WIgVxM39sZE
  • Source page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WIgVxM39sZE

One-goalie / single-net additions (added 2026-10-06)

For nights with only ONE netminder: single-net small-area games (second net replaced by tires, gates or passing targets), one-net stations that rotate shooters, no-goalie stations, and goalie workload references. Every plan file now has a `## One-goalie option` section that uses these. Videos were checked against their title/description (YouTube oEmbed + page text) or are the video embedded on the drill's own IHS page.

39. 2 vs 2 Game (With 1 Goalie & Tire Nets)

  • Tags: `sag|one-goalie`
  • Directions: Cross-ice game built for nights with one goalie: one team shoots on the goalie while the other team scores by hitting 1–3 tires set at the opposite end (more tires = easier). Coach flips a puck in on the whistle; change on a goal, a freeze, a puck out of play, or the whistle. Switch sides during the game (or every time the tire team scores) so everyone gets to attack the goalie. Scales to 2v2, 3v3 or 4v4.
  • Video: https://vimeo.com/657484569 (note: Vimeo file is embed-restricted (plays on the IHS page, not on vimeo.com).)
  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/2-vs-2-game-1-goalie-tire-nets

40. Back to Back Nets – One Goalie (wall shooters)

  • Tags: `sag|one-goalie|goalie`
  • Directions: Nets back-to-back in the middle of the zone with ONE goalie covering both. Play 2v2 or 3v3; each team has a designated player on its offensive wall and must pass to that player to go on offense — the wall player can shoot or pass. A drawn line can keep defenders off the wall players. Designed for one-goalie practices and adds goalie skating/recovery reps (keep shifts short so it stays quality, not chaos).
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J66B2W1FF4E
  • Source page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J66B2W1FF4E

41. 2v2 Tight Area in Corner (1 Goalie)

  • Tags: `sag|contact|one-goalie`
  • Directions: Place a net in the corner on an angle facing the slot and use boards/dividers to confine a small area that keeps pucks in. Play 2v2 in 45-second shifts and keep score. Only one net is live, so a single goalie handles it while the game teaches core offensive and defensive habits in tight space (support, protection, stick on puck, net-front).
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V97nywNK4lo
  • Source page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V97nywNK4lo

42. Goal Line Small Area Game (USA Hockey)

  • Tags: `sag|contact|one-goalie`
  • Directions: Draw a line across the corner about 6 ft behind the net; two players per team play 2v2 on a single net with a neutral goalie. Coach spots a loose puck to start a battle. On every change of possession the puck must be carried or passed below the goal line before the new team can attack. Coach defensive-side body position, stick on puck and awareness away from the puck; offensively, puck protection and support.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nFqJT564ZgQ
  • Source page: https://www.usahockey.com/smallareagames

43. 3 vs 3 Split Zone Game

  • Tags: `sag|systems|one-goalie`
  • Directions: Split one zone in half lengthwise; 3 forwards attack one net (one goalie) against 3 defenders. Coach chips the puck to the goalie, who directs it to the corner to start. Forwards earn 2 points for a goal; defenders earn 1 point by completing one pass and then exiting the zone. The rep ends on a goal, an exit, a goalie freeze or the whistle.

44. 3 on 2 Race to 5 (Cail MacLean)

  • Tags: `sag|systems|one-goalie`
  • Directions: Below the tops of the circles: 3 forwards vs 2 defensemen plus the goalie. Coach dumps a puck and the rep plays 10–20 seconds. Forwards get 1 point for a goal; defenders get 1 point for skating the puck past the line; the goalie's side gets 1 point for covering the puck. New players on every point; first to 5 wins.

45. Tomas Holmstrom SAG (net-front)

  • Tags: `sag|goalie|one-goalie`
  • Directions: Mark a box from just inside the dots/hash marks up to the tops of the circles. Three attackers vs two (or three) defenders battle inside it while a shooter at the top of the circles fires 5 pucks in a row — shots only (no direct passes), and only after the whistle. On each whistle attackers must tag up outside the box and re-win inside position for screens, tips and rebounds; defenders box out and block. Switch after 5 reps and keep score.

46. 2v2 Block Out Battle (Hockey Coach Vision)

  • Tags: `sag|contact|goalie|one-goalie`
  • Directions: Coach shoots off the goalie's pads to create a rebound; forwards attack the loose puck while defenders box them out. On the next whistle the forwards race around the cones and a second puck starts a 2v2 battle down low. Cue defenders to keep their body between man and net, forwards to fight for inside position, and everyone to talk.

47. Gretzky 3 vs 2 Behind the Net

  • Tags: `sag|systems|one-goalie`
  • Directions: Tops of the circles and below, one net. Coach dumps a puck and names one team to send 3 players and the other 2. The team of 3 must always keep one player below the goal line; if that forward comes up, the puck has to go behind the net to the next forward rotating down. Defenders communicate switches and control body and stick.

48. 3 v 2 Dot Jumper

  • Tags: `sag|systems|one-goalie`
  • Directions: Coach chips a puck to start a 2v2 race; one extra player from each team skates straight to a faceoff dot and must stay there until receiving a pass. The team with possession can pass to its dot player to make it 3v2; if the defenders steal it, they activate their own dot player. One net in-zone — emphasize moving without the puck, communication and following shots.

49. Swiss 4 vs 2 Scoring Game

  • Tags: `sag|systems|one-goalie`
  • Directions: Divide the offensive zone with a line through the dots (or hash marks/cones) into a high and a low area, each holding a 2v1 — four attackers vs two defenders on one net. Defenders must stay in their area with an active stick; attackers can pass anywhere and must shoot within about 5 seconds. Change on a miss, freeze or puck out; rotate low attackers out, defenders to the low attack spots, high attackers to defense.

50. Pass-to-Score 2v2 / 2v1 Games (one goalie)

  • Tags: `sag|skills|one-goalie`
  • Directions: Game 1: 2v2 between the blue line and a drawn line; a team can only score after passing to its own moving outlet player in a separate lane, and on a turnover the other team must hit its outlet first. Game 2: in a roped-off area a 2v1 (or 3v2) plays first-to-3 — tape-to-tape forehand passes score for the attackers, any touch scores for the defender — and the winners get a 2-on-0 (or partial breakaway) on the goalie. The goalie only sees the reward rush, so his reps stay high quality.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZkkZ5L1volI
  • Source page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZkkZ5L1volI

51. Sticks In Lanes Game (Topher Scott)

  • Tags: `sag|systems|one-goalie`
  • Directions: Six attackers hold set spots around the zone (they can shift but not skate around) against two defenders in the middle; one net. The offense must pass through the middle of the ice two or more times before it can shoot; defenders keep sticks on the ice to block lanes and break up plays. Switch teams every rep and keep score. Harder: 4v2, 6v3, a smaller area, or 3 passes through the middle.

  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/sticks-lanes-game

52. Power Play Scoring Competition (Wes Wolfe)

  • Tags: `systems|one-goalie`
  • Directions: Half-ice with one goalie: a 5-man power play enters off a coach pass and plays 60 seconds. It starts 5-on-0 for 15 s, then the coach whistles in one penalty killer every 15 s until it finishes 5-on-4. New puck immediately after a goal or freeze (vary rims and bouncing pucks); each unit gets three 60-s rounds and the unit with the most goals wins.
  • Video: https://vimeo.com/1045818627 (note: Vimeo file is embed-restricted (plays on the IHS page).)

53. Horseshoe Regroup 2-on-1 (one goalie)

  • Tags: `systems|skills|one-goalie`
  • Directions: One-goalie regroup series: forwards exchange passes up the ice, the first forward drives for a shot and rebound while the second cuts across, takes a pass and moves it D-to-D through the defense. The last defenseman to touch it steps up over the blue line and gets back into position to defend the 2-on-1 into the same net. Cue tape-to-tape passes, driving the net, and the defender's gap after the step-up.

54. Half Ice Shoot In Stride

  • Tags: `skills|goalie|one-goalie`
  • Directions: Two lines at the hash marks; the first player skates toward the red line and the opposite coach, calls for a puck, receives it with feet moving and shoots in stride before the cone, then stops at the net for a rebound. Alternate lines so the goalie sees one shot at a time from varied angles. Cue verbal and stick-target communication and shooting without stopping the feet.

55. The Gate Game (no goalie)

  • Tags: `sag|skills|one-goalie`
  • Directions: Set three gates with heavy tires or cones; play 3v3 where a team scores by passing through a gate to a teammate on the other side. Whoever wins the puck is on offense — no net, no goalie. It forces players to spread out and move the puck fast; make it easier with more/wider gates or add a blue-line passer for a 4v3 feel.

  • Source page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bHTPn2TsmFQ

56. Nowak No-Goalie Transition Game

  • Tags: `sag|contact|one-goalie`
  • Directions: 1v1 in the middle with support players on each wall and a cone gate at center ice. The puck carrier regroups with the wall players to get the puck across to the other side: carry it across outside the cones = 1 point, between the cones = 2 points. Wall players may pass to the other player on the same wall but not across the ice. No goalie needed.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cc1xg7o1weo
  • Source page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cc1xg7o1weo

57. Gates Passing Small Area Game (partners)

  • Tags: `skills|warm-up|one-goalie`
  • Directions: Pairs share one puck inside a zone filled with cone gates. Pass to your partner through a gate, then both move to a new gate; you can't use the same gate twice in a row. Play for time and count gates completed per pair — heads up, move to open ice, communicate.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cq7SUFsoU0Q
  • Source page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cq7SUFsoU0Q

58. 2vs2 Shooting Board Game (IIHF Skills4Life)

  • Tags: `sag|contact|one-goalie`
  • Directions: Teams wait above the faceoff circles; play 2v2 in front of the net area with a shooting board for each team at the top of the circle instead of a goalie. The coach on the blue line plays a puck in to start; change on the coach's signal. Defending focus: stay between opponent and goal, cut off passing lanes, play the body, apply stick pressure and be ready for the loose puck.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tjsSHPu_eWU
  • Source page: https://www.iihf.com/en/coaching/18952/2vs2-shooting-board

59. 1vs1 Three-Gate Game (IIHF Skills4Life)

  • Tags: `contact|skills|one-goalie`
  • Directions: 1v1 inside a faceoff circle with three gates on the rim. The puck carrier tries to carry the puck out through any gate against a defender; on a turnover roles flip immediately. Teaches winning space with skating and deception, protecting the puck with body position, and readiness to regain possession. No goalie needed.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FRqZepqBTlI
  • Source page: https://www.iihf.com/en/coaching/19068/1vs1-three-gate-game

60. Neutral Zone Passing Station #1

  • Tags: `skills|warm-up|one-goalie`
  • Directions: Three side-by-side passing lanes in the neutral zone (or two longer lanes for fewer players) so six players go at once. Partners make one pass between each set of cones; at the last cone they turn toward each other, switch sides with a drop pass to the partner's forehand, and pass between each cone on the way back. Switch sides every rep for forehand and backhand reps.

  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/neutral-zone-passing-station-1

61. Transition Pivot Races

  • Tags: `skills|one-goalie`
  • Directions: Two teams line up on either side of the center circle; coach at center with pucks. On the whistle skate forward until both feet are inside the blue line, pivot backward to a cone, pivot forward around it and back into the zone, then pivot backward to the second cone at center, open up to forward and race to the puck the coach places near the blue line. Open the hips without crossing over; the race adds urgency to footwork.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nsBIiBy02Mw
  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/transition-pivot-hockey-races

62. Circle 2v1 / Keep-Away Series (1 or 0 goalies)

  • Tags: `skills|sag|one-goalie`
  • Directions: Version 1: two attackers stay behind a drawn line and pass through a faceoff circle (one defender inside with an active stick) for one-timers. Version 2: 2v1, 2v2 or 3v1 inside the circle using the circle edge or bumpers as the boundary. Version 3: monkey-in-the-middle with passers on the rim moving the puck quickly around 1–2 defenders inside (4v2). Versions 2–3 run with no goalie at all.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RyLQIUL6Pek
  • Source page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RyLQIUL6Pek

63. Tire Deke & Shoot Station

  • Tags: `skills|one-goalie`
  • Directions: Players skate with a puck, deke around a tire, and take a quick shot on goal in a continuous, high-rep station. On one-goalie nights shoot into a shooter tutor, an upside-down net, or tires/targets in an empty net so the goalie is free for another station. Cue head up on the approach and release in stride after the deke.

64. Upside-Down Net Target Shooting (no goalie)

  • Tags: `skills|one-goalie`
  • Directions: When there is no goalie for a station, lay a spare net on its back and push it against the standing net so only a narrow strip near the crossbar stays open. Players shoot and finish at the small target, which rewards elevating the puck under control and keeps shooting stations alive without a netminder. Pucks only — nobody stands in the crease.

65. Shooting Recovery Drill (2 shooters, goalie reset)

  • Tags: `goalie|one-goalie`
  • Directions: Goalie-specific drill from the OHL Coaches Conference clip: two shooters alternate — a low shot, the goalie recovers to his feet and sets on the next shooter — then progress to setting up on the rebound before moving to the next shooter. Short, controlled reps that build recovery and tracking habits. Ideal for the goalie's first 2–3 minutes of shots while skaters run a no-goalie station.

66. Goalie Workload: Engage Goalies at Practice (USA Hockey)

  • Tags: `goalie|one-goalie`
  • Directions: USA Hockey coaching tip: give goalies a real warm-up at the start (goalie coach or an assistant) and choose team drills that train game situations, such as stopping/setting pucks behind the net in 2-on-1s. Pair it with USA Hockey's goaltending guidance: quality of reps over quantity, let the goalie reset and track the rebound between shots, and in high-volume drills let them hop out for a few reps — skaters shooting at an empty net for a few reps doesn't ruin the drill.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=g-GT6LRA9Nw
  • Source page: https://www.usahockey.com/news_article/show/1352978

67. Goalie Workload: Preparing Goalies for Practice (Jeff Lerg)

  • Tags: `goalie|one-goalie`
  • Directions: The Coaches Site talk by Jeff Lerg: in a poll of 153 goalies most wanted a warm-up with a coach first and preferred small-area games later, after they had seen pucks. Goalie reps should include pre-shot movement, lateral plays and traffic like real games; when ice is limited, a coach can work the goalie in a corner while the team runs a no-goalie or one-goalie game. Goalies own their movement warm-up while skaters warm up.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ocit0BtG3Sw
  • Source page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ocit0BtG3Sw

68. Goalie Workload: Goalie-Friendly Practice (FutureProGoaltending)

  • Tags: `goalie|one-goalie`
  • Directions: Advice for head coaches on not wearing goalies out in practice: drop rapid-fire drills, build a gap between shots so the goalie can track the rebound into the corner, and train in proportion to games (more zone-play looks, fewer endless line rushes and slappers from the top of the circles). Make warm-ups for the goalie, not the shooters, and occasionally track practice save percentage so every puck matters.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ywcijl1ak_c
  • Source page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ywcijl1ak_c
